alerts.reason: September-quarter revenue grew just $11 million year over year, versus $166 million of growth across the first half, calculated from the $177 million nine-month gain (A). Hot-rolled coil prices fell 22% sequentially (C). If lower steel prices feed through to selling prices over several months, I expect revenue growth to stay above -5% in December and fall to -5% or worse in March.

September net sales fell 2.2% despite higher customer pricing and favorable FX (A). Two plant closures reduced volume (C). I expect pricing to keep the December decline under 5%, with continuing volume losses pushing the March decline to at least 5% if pricing offsets less of the loss.

September net sales fell 3.8%, just 1.2 percentage points short of the threshold (A). Astec still had $614.7 million of orders to ship, but backlog was down $354.3 million year over year (B, C). I expect existing orders to cushion December sales and the smaller backlog to push the March sales decline to at least 5%.

September-quarter net bookings fell year over year (B). The weakness extended beyond older releases to NBA 2K and several mobile franchises (E). I expect the bookings shortfall to reach reported revenue with a lag, leaving December revenue growth above -5% before a March decline of at least 5%.

September operating revenue fell 1.2% year over year (A). One-Way Truckload faced less available freight and spot-rate pressure, and its revenue per total mile excluding fuel surcharges fell 4.8% (B, D). I expect the consolidated decline to remain under 5% in December and reach at least 5% in March as fewer loads compound lower rates.

Passenger traffic rose 11% while yield fell 10%, implying nearly flat passenger revenue as demand softened (B). I expect traffic growth to keep the December total revenue decline, if any, under 5%. If yield stays down 10%, traffic growth below roughly 5.6% would put passenger revenue down at least 5%, supporting a March crossing in total revenue.
